A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SongBloom research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original objective and listening-test evaluations, diffusion-condition ablations, hyperparameter experiments, and sketch-representation results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds objective and subjective evaluations of Mureka-O1 in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The interleaved sketch/acoustic generation procedure, architecture, conditioning, and training objectives remain unchanged. Section 4.2's revised continuous-latent explanation describes a representation already present in v1; both versions identify the same waveform autoencoder implementation in Section 5.2.

E1.justification: Both retain the 100K-hour Chinese/English song training coverage and evaluation using generated lyrics and reference clips from unseen songs. The revised synthetic fine-tuning data description does not establish a new dataset, task, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Mureka-O1 is added to both the objective and subjective comparisons in Tables 2–3, using a 10-second audio prompt. All previous comparators remain; ACE-step was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes the stated FAD reference from real song clips to the real songs from which those clips are taken. This is a limited reported evaluation-setting revision, without evidence that scores were recomputed. Other stated training budgets, model configurations, and listening-test procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diffusion-condition ablations in Table 4, patch-size and diffusion-step analyses in Figures 2–3, and sketch-representation ablations in Appendix A/Table 5 are retained with the same results. No new robustness or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same MOS reporting with ± quantities; Mureka-O1 follows that existing practice. Neither version adds a definition of the uncertainty statistic, repeated-run or seed information, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 add Mureka-O1 results, including PER 7.79%, MCC 0.86, FAD 3.39, and vocal musicality 3.91 ± 0.26. Its vocal musicality mean ties SongBloom-full-ft, while its accompaniment mean is 3.93 versus 3.92. Existing numerical entries, ablation results, and appendix findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and Appendix B's inference-complexity assumptions, derivation, and efficiency condition are unchanged. The revised FAD reference description introduces no new mathematical definition or theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and concluding discussion retain the same claims about the unified autoregressive diffusion framework, interleaved generation, competitive song quality, and inference efficiency. Adding Mureka-O1 evidence does not revise these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 changes the fine-tuning explanation from emulating Suno-style compositions to emulating synthesized lyric compositions, emphasizing alternating verses and choruses. Other mechanism explanations and Section 7 limitations remain unchanged, including the superiority discussion that is not updated for Mureka-O1.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link on page 1. Section 6.1 adds structural detail about fine-tuning data but removes their explicit Suno provenance; Section 4.2 also drops the statement that the authors train the autoencoder specifically on music. Existing hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the ACE-step paper as reference 45 and cites it in Tables 2–3, where the baseline already appeared in v1. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the acoustic-representation, FAD, and fine-tuning passages, plus small terminology corrections such as changing 'small batch size' to 'small patch size' in Section 6.3. The section order and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain Mureka-O1 rows and move ACE-step into the open-source block. Captions for Tables 2–4 move above the tables, and Figure 1's legend specifies '(compressed) acoustic token.' Other displays remain substantially unchanged, including the appendix pages.

improvement.justification: The added Mureka-O1 comparisons and code link improve comparative evidence and access information. However, v3 removes explicit fine-tuning data provenance and retains the claim that SongBloom and Suno outperform all other models by a clear margin, despite Mureka-O1 tying SongBloom-full-ft's vocal musicality mean and slightly exceeding its accompaniment mean. These benefits coexist with reduced transparency and an unreconciled results interpretation, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
